function.name: start_auction
function.arguments: {"public_message": "Kentucky Avenue goes to auction. I don't need it—my infrastructure is already locked. Let the table bid against itself while I preserve capital for the properties that actually matter. The railroads and utilities are where this game is won, and you're all still chasing colors.", "private_thought": "Kentucky Avenue is a red property ($220 cost). I own 0/3 reds—no monopoly path here. My strategy is railroads (Reading Railroad acquired) + utilities (Electric Company acquired) + completing the railroad set (Pennsylvania Railroad, Short Line). Red properties are low-priority; they generate modest rent ($18-$1050 with full build-out) but require heavy capital investment in houses/hotels. Current cash: $1150. Spending $220 here weakens my position for acquiring Pennsylvania Railroad ($200) and Short Line ($200), which are critical for railroad monopoly ($200 rent per landing). Auction forces opponents to bid against each other, burning their cash while I preserve liquidity. Gemini ($1380) and Grok ($1300) are cash-rich; let them waste capital on secondary properties. GPT ($1060) is cash-constrained and won't bid aggressively. Auction is the optimal play: deny myself a weak property, force opponents into wasteful spending, and maintain cash superiority for infrastructure acquisition. Stay in control. End turn with $1150 cash intact."}
